item.title: Joe Burrow lifts Bengals past Falcons in Spain - Reactions
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had 271 passing yards with three touchdown passes during the team's NFL Week 9 win against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals improved to 6-2 this season. Burrow would have become the third quarterback in NFL history to throw four or more touchdown passes in four consecutive games, but came up one passing TD short. The only two QBs to achieve that feat, per NBC Sports, were Indianapolis Colts quarterback Peyton Manning in 2004 and Miami Dolphins quarterback Dan Marino in 1984. Burrow has 16 passing TDs over the past four games. Burrow added a rushing TD against Atlanta, and reacted with a unique celebration . Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins celebrated Chase's first-quarter TD with a bullfighting nod . Higgins handed the ball to an excited young fan after recording his 50th career TD . During analysis on NFL Network before the game, Pro Football Hall of Famer Kurt Warner said he thinks his NFL Most Valuable Player pick, Burrow, can lead Cincinnati back to the Super Bowl. The linebacker has been in the hospital since, but he released a statement saying that he has regained movement in his lower body and is making progress in his upper body. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. item.description: NFL insider would be 'floored' if Chiefs don't make this one move by NFL trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs are in the market for help at a few different positions as the 2026 NFL trade deadline nears. But wide receiver is their obvious top need. After losing Tyquan Thornton for the season, it's painfully obvious that this team needs WR help. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy aren't good enough. That's why the Chiefs have been linked to so many wide receivers this season. But will they land a WR in a trade by Tuesday's deadline? NFL insider Jonathan Jones of The Athletic revealed that he would be "floored" if the Chiefs don't find a way to upgrade their WR room, which is a good sign for Chiefs fans. NFL insider would be 'floored' if Chiefs don't trade for a WR "The Chiefs continue to search for wide receiver help," Jones reports. "... I will be floored if they don't have someone by Tuesday evening." While Jones doesn't note what kind of wide receiver upgrade or addition the Chiefs are likely to make, he does believe a move of some kind is coming. Kansas City needs WR help, and some very intriguing top-tier options might actually be available for trade that would be huge boosts for this Chiefs offense. Brian Thomas Jr. is one name to watch, as the Jacksonville Jaguars might move the former first-round pick. George Pickens from the Dallas Cowboys is another, as he might be dealt as well. There are plenty of other depth options worth keeping tabs on as well. The Chiefs seem likely to add at least something to their wide receiver room by the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday evening. Whether it's a star player or not remains to be seen, but it looks likely Patrick Mahomes will have a new target by Week 10. item.title: Detroit Red Wings demote Nate Danielson among other re-assignments
item.description: This fall was a golden opportunity for Nate Danielson, but his inability to cash in led to a demotion. The 2023 first-round pick was assigned by the Detroit Red Wings to the Grand Rapids Griffins on Sunday, Nov. 8, along with goaltender Michal Postava and forward John Leonard. Postava's re-assignment was expected, as John Gibson has healed from the lower-body injury that forced him to leave after the first period against the Tampa Bay Lightning on Nov. 3. Leonard's re-assignment is an indication either or both of Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton, out for a month with injuries, are ready to return when the Wings next play, Tuesday at the St. Louis Blues . [ Red Wings' promise vs top teams should spark some sort of Larkin move ] Danielson being included in the group isn't a surprise, either, but it is not a good development for the young forward. The 22-year-old, drafted at No. 9 overall three years ago, had a great chance as the Wings began 2026-27 to grab a spot, what with the Wings in desperate need of someone to step up at center, where they are thin on depth and with Dylan Larkin suspended by the team . But Danielson never showed the assertiveness the Wings needed to see from him. He was in and out of the lineup as a result, and had just two points, both assists, and a minus-7 rating after 13 appearances. TRENDING: Wings 'didn't deal well with our emotions' in Colorado The Wings did not practice Sunday, but coach Todd McLellan spoke about Danielson (6 feet 2, 196 pounds) a couple of weeks ago. "He's a really good, honest player," McLellan said Oct. 21. "He wants to do well. I think sometimes you play so that you don't err. That's probably not the best way of approaching it." The Wings wanted to see Danielson establish his value in the lineup the way Michael Brandsegg-Nygard and Anton Johansson have come in and done this fall, but given his struggles to do so, Danielson will now continue his development in the minors. item.title: Alcaraz beats Shelton in Paris to secure first Masters title of season
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz arrives on the black carpet for Laver Cup Opening Night at Magazine London. (is associated with: «Alcaraz beats Shelton in Paris to secure first Masters title of season») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz won a rematch against Ben Shelton to claim his first Masters 1,000 title of the season in Paris on Sunday. Alcaraz lost out in a memorable late-night epic against American Shelton in the quarter-finals of the US Open in his first tournament back after four and a half months out with a wrist injury. But the Spaniard has quickly found his form and made it back-to-back titles after winning in Vienna last week with a 7-6 (7-5), 7-5 victory in the French capital. It is the first time for more than a year that Alcaraz has won a title at the top level of the ATP Tour, and a particularly notable one given he had previously struggled at the event. Addressing his team at the presentation ceremony, Alcaraz said: “This is something that we’ve been chasing for a really long time. “Not finding the great feeling coming here every year, not finding my great tennis, but we never give up. I had really painful losses here but we tried and tried again and finally we felt really comfortable coming here.” It was not a classic match but once again it was Alcaraz who came out on top in the crucial moments, notably edging a first-set tie-break after withstanding some fierce pressure on his serve. Big-serving Shelton, who continues to demonstrate his improvement, secured the first break of serve of the match to lead 4-2 in the second set but Alcaraz hit back strongly, winning five of the next six games. Shelton praised his opponent, saying: “I don’t think that everybody realizes how difficult it is go back-to-back in Vienna and Paris. Ten matches in 14 days, going from a slow court to a very fast court. “I think it speaks to your versatility as a champion and the work that you and your team put in. Every time we’re on the court together I feel you bring out the best in me. I’m super happy to have you back and healthy.”

item.description: Kenneth Walker III and the Kansas City Chiefs suffered their second straight loss in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos. It was a competitive game from start to finish, including some penalty flags thrown. One of them was when the running back was grabbed by Eyioma Uwazurike via a facemask. The Chiefs had a chance to extend their lead to six points late in the fourth quarter. However, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal attempt wide right, giving the home team good field position. Bo Nix and Co. took advantage of it, scoring a touchdown in only 35 second in the ensuing drive. Patrick Mahomes led Kansas City with 30-of-41 completions for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions in the 28-24 defeat. Walker finished with 21 rushes for 69 yards, while the receiving corps saw another running back record the most yardage. Emmett Johnson amassed five catches for 128 yards and one score. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) reacts after scoring a touchdown against the Denver Broncos at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. NFL Issues Fine on Eyioma Uwazurike for Kenneth Walker III Facemask The NFL released its accountability list for Week 8. Eyioma Uwazurike has been handed a $6,361 fine for his penalty on Kenneth Walker III. Denver also placed him on short-term injured reserve on Saturday. item.title: Sergio Garcia finally speaks out about his appalling behavior at Augusta National this year
item.description: Photo by Augusta National/Augusta National/Getty Images Sergio Garcia has the privilege of returning to Augusta National every year to compete in The Masters after he won the tournament way back in 2017. However, Garcia came close to losing that privilege after his appalling behavior at Augusta National during the final round of The Masters this year. The Spaniard let loose on the second tee box at Augusta after flaring his drive out to the right, repeatedly striking the ground with his club before unleashing his anger on a water cooler. Sergio Garcia was warned about his behavior by Augusta National officials , although many believed he should have faced a more severe punishment. Garcia ‘s arrogant and, quite frankly, carefree behavior during his post-match press conference did him no favors either. The 2017 Masters champion did not even apologize for his actions. However, the Spaniard has finally taken full accountability for his actions at Augusta National back in April. Sergio Garcia speaks out about his poor behavior at Augusta National Garcia has irked many golf fans, analysts and his fellow players over the past few years with some truly horrendous behavior on the golf course. The 46-year-old from Spain clearly has serious issues with his temper and he regularly displays angry outbursts during tournaments. There is no better example of that than Garcia’s shocking behavior at Augusta National this year, and now the Spaniard has finally admitted that he is working very hard on controlling his temper. “Yeah I am obviously very disappointed in myself at what happened there,” Garcia told Golf Magic . “There were some things going on that obviously didn’t help me off the golf course, and that kind of showed up with my frustration on the course. ”The only thing I can do is learn from it, work on it, which I’m doing. I am working really hard on it and the mental side of it, and becoming better and better on and off the golf course. “That’s the only thing I can do at the end of the day, and then my actions will show if I am improving or not, it’s as simple as that. The only thing I can do is keep working on it and show everyone that I’m getting better and better at it.” As Sergio Garcia said, actions speak louder than words. So, we will see over the course of the next year or so whether he has actually changed. One thing’s for sure, if he repeats his behavior during The Masters at Augusta National ever again, he may never be welcomed back.

item.title: Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman’s message to CFP committee after Miami win cold takes initial ranking snub
item.description: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman’s message to CFP committee after Miami win cold takes initial ranking snub appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the biggest surprises of the initial College Football Playoff rankings last Tuesday was the placement of Notre Dame. The Irish, despite a 7-1 record and a sterling history of laying waste to inferior opponents, came in at No. 11 in the rankings , right on the projected cut line. The selection committee sent Notre Dame a message: win against No. 1 Miami on Saturday night, or you are likely out. Marcus Freeman and company answered the bell, getting a 31-24 win over the top-ranked team in the country in South Bend and sending a message that they are national title contenders in the process. After the game, Freeman talked about using that initial ranking, which came as a shock to many, as motivation coming into this game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We learned that last year, it doesn’t matter what you’re ranked until the last week, and that’s the truth,” Freeman said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. “We don’t need to focus on it. We don’t need to talk about it. Our job was to leave no doubt today, and they [did not].” A loss would have put Notre Dame in a very similar situation as it was in last season, when the Irish blew out 10 inferior teams but lost to both Miami and Texas A&M, a pair of playoff teams. The committee judged that since Notre Dame didn’t have quality wins, it was less deserving of a spot than Alabama or Miami, and the Irish were the first team on the outside looking in. The Hurricanes made good on that decision with their run all the way to the national championship game. Now, Notre Dame doesn’t have to worry about a similar scenario playing out this season. The Irish have three games remaining in the regular season, and if Freeman and company can take care of business in those games, they will be securely in the CFP. Notre Dame will be back in action next Saturday against Boston College, and a marquee matchup with an explosive SMU team looms in Week 12 as the final big test of the regular season. item.description: NFL teams ‘certain’ Jaguars will make obvious decision on Brian Thomas Jr. trade rumors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars could have one of the more fun trade deadlines of any team in the NFL this season. With a strong record and a path to the AFC's No. 1 seed, this Jaguars team could make a push for a true star-level player this season. But the Jaguars might not only make a splash as buyers. They could also make a huge move as sellers. Brian Thomas Jr. is a name floating around the NFL right now as an intriguing trade target for wide receiver-needy teams. While Jacksonville has rebuffed trade rumors, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones is reporting that the NFL sees this situation differently. The NFL "seems certain" that the Jaguars will trade Thomas this season, as the third-year WR could be gone by Tuesday. NFL 'seems certain' that the Jaguars will trade Brian Thomas Jr. "The Jaguars have held firm in keeping wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. We'll see if they keep that posture after Thursday," Jones writes. "The rest of the league seems certain the Jags will part with Thomas." What this report from Jones indicates is that those around the NFL believe the Jaguars turning down any notion of a Thomas trade is all posturing, and that the third-year WR will be on the move this season. It's such an obvious move for the Jaguars that it would be a bit of a surprise to see him not traded away. Sure, the Jaguars are contenders, and having extra WR help couldn't hurt. But Thomas has fallen to fourth on the depth chart at best. Maybe they use him to acquire Moro Ojomo or someone like Jalen Carter from the Philadelphia Eagles . Or maybe they splurge on a good defensive tackle and use a Thomas trade to recoup some of the draft compensation they lost in that trade. The NFL believes the Jaguars are going to trade Thomas, and with all of the rumors going around, it wouldn't be a surprise to see him go at all. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. during Friday Night Lights training camp practice at Latrobe Memorial Stadium on Aug. 2, 2024. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Former Pittsburgh Steelers George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. have been ruled out for the Dallas Cowboys in Sunday’s Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts. He was limited in all three practice sessions this week before being ruled questionable on Friday. Pickens’ injury could prevent him from being traded at Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline , if that’s something the Cowboys would have interest in doing. He’s currently playing under the franchise tag, and is scheduled to become a free agent in March. There has been little talk of news on him signing a contract extension with the Cowboys recently. With Pickens out, Ryan Flournoy will likely step into a larger role alongside fellow starter CeeDee Lamb. Kick returner and slot receiver KaVonte Turpin has also been ruled out. Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. during a game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Porter was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, but was listed as limited on Thursday and Friday. He is also in the final year of his contract — the rookie deal he signed in Pittsburgh — and also has not had any progress toward signing an extension in Dallas. item.title: Casey Mears makes milestone 500th NASCAR Cup start he never meant to reach
item.description: Motorsport photo Between Feb. 16, 2003 and Nov. 8, 2026, Casey Mears made 500 NASCAR Cup starts, and in doing so, becomes just the 50th driver in NASCAR Cup history to reach 500 starts. “I just feel really appreciative of the opportunity,” said Mears going into the race weekend. “I’d say it’s pretty rare that somebody gets to be out of the sport for that long and then comes back and participates. I’m excited to go do it one last time.” Never planned to make 500 NASCAR Cup starts Casey Mears, No. 66 Garage 66 Ford Casey Mears, No. 66 Garage 66 Ford Mears never expected to reach this milestone, seemingly ending his career after the 2016 season. He showed up in the Daytona 500 three years later for his 490th start, and that appeared to be the end of his time in NASCAR. But the surprise that Mears has made it this far goes beyond that, as his original plan for a NASCAR career did not span 23 years. When he moved to North Carolina from California, Mears says: "I honestly felt like I was going to try this NASCAR thing out, get a taste of it, and probably end up going back to IndyCar." It made sense for Mears to pursue open-wheel as the nephew of legendary four-time Indy 500 winner Rick Mears. He had already made five starts in CART and three in IndyCar during the split era, finishing fourth on debut at Fontana. His first-ever appearance in the national levels of NASCAR came at Homestead in 2001, driving the No. 66 Cicci-Welliver Racing in a NASCAR O'Reilly race. His Cup career began in 2003, driving the No. 41 Chip Ganassi Racing Dodge in the Daytona 500, placing 27th. As fate would have it, he never did go back to IndyCar, competing full-time in the Cup Series in all but one year between 2003 and 2016. Defining moment of NASCAR career Victory lane: race winner Casey Mears celebrates Victory lane: race winner Casey Mears celebrates As an up-and-coming racer, he dreamed of winning on Memorial Day weekend, but that dream involved a yard of bricks and a glass of milk. He did end up winning on that special race weekend, but it was the defining moment of a career in NASCAR -- not IndyCar. Now driving for Hendrick Motorsports , he won the 2007 Coca-Cola 600 in a fuel-mileage gamble, leading just the final six laps of the race. Xabi Alonso's Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish. Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season. Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Alonso. Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill. "We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there," Alonso said. "You can do it, we spoke and worked. We didn't do good enough but we worked during the week to control their powers. For sure in a few situations we didn't do well." Liverpool had been beaten by Arsenal in the Premier League and Fenerbahce in the Champions League before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager's first season in charge at Anfield. But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front at Selhurst Park from Dominik Szoboszlai's cross after 40 minutes. Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool's second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola's cross in the 54th minute. It was Wirtz's first league goal this season and only the second in all competitions for the inconsistent German playmaker this term. Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz's pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool's much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak. It was Liverpool's fourth consecutive away league win this season. Eddie Nketiah's stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for Palace. Palace manager Pierre Sage -- hired to replace Oliver Glasner in the close-season is on the brink of being sacked after his side slumped to the bottom of the table following their seventh defeat in 10 league matches. "It was an important win for us going into the international break after the week we've had," Iraola said.
